transcript: There's a great new play at the Connolly Theater Upstairs right now called Pre-Existing Condition by Marin Ireland. It’s a series of scenes centered around a woman in the aftermath of having been in a violent relationship as she interacts with lawyers, counselors, friends, family, etc. Though the content warning definitely feels apt, the overall tone of the piece was not as cathartic as I expected based on the subject matter. It’s really just a portrait of the kaleidoscopic complexities of processing trauma. I also thought the way this piece explored the social implications and stigmas that people can experience following traumatic events was quite moving. With a small set of actresses playing the lead in rotation and the theater seating just 60 people a night, I'm sure each and every performance is a unique experience. The night I saw it, the show was led by Tony Award winner Deirdre O'Connell. Her performance was subtle and understated, quietly heartbreaking, very impactful in a small space. Needless to say, I enjoyed. With that, another program for my collection.
